findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed member of staff to wash hands and not use a barrier to turn off faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off faucet after handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be hot holding between 110-125F. Discussed with PIC, items were over to stovetop to reheat to 165F and steam table was turned to a hotter temperature. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Observed the following items to be missing date marking:
1) (Repeat) Open cakes stored with no date marking present. 
2) Sauces in the walk in cooler. 

Discussed with PIC, cakes were purchased/made this week and the proper date marking was placed on cakes and sauces. Ensure any open TCS food held longer than 24 hours has the proper date marking available.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed multiple items ranging from soups, sauces, and other TCS items to be resting/cooling on the floor in kitchen line and walk in cooler. Discussed with staff, all containers were moved to at least 6 inches off of floor. Ensure all foods are kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed single service plates to be stored not inverted on shelf. Discussed with PIC, plates were inverted. Ensure plates are stored in way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed a leak to be present at server station hand sink. Discussed with PIC, a replacement part has been ordered. Ensure no leaks are present at hand sink.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed PIC to wash hands for 2 seconds without soap use. Discussed with PIC, inspector attempted to offer education on proper hand washing education. Ensure any food employees washes hands for at least 20 seconds without soap use the use of a cleaning compound.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed PIC to not use a barrier after the attempted hand wash. Discussed with PIC, education was again attempted to be provided. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off faucet after hand washing to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed PIC to be bare handling hash browns cooking on stovetop. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on bare hand contact with exposed foods and PIC was instructed to wash hands and use gloves in the future. Ensure employees minimize bare hand contact with exposed foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, the sanitizer set up to dish machine had run out. A new bottle was switched out and dish machine tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizing dish machine is testing at the proper concentration to ensure dishes are properly being wash, rinsed, and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed food debris buildup to be present under the left prep cooler lid in cook line. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.comment: Observed soup to be cooling at 100F after 1.5 hours. Discussed with PIC, soup will be constantly stirred and moved to walk in cooler to drop temperature quicker. Ensure all TCS foods being cooled are at 70F after 2 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed precooked sausages to be hot held at 90F. Discussed with PIC, TCS items were pulled from hot holding and cooked to 165F before returning to hot holding. Ensure any TCS food being hot held to be kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed soup to be cooling at 100F in ambient air temperature. Discussed with PIC, inspector provided education regarding proper cooling techniques. Ensure staff is properly monitoring cooling.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed ice scoop to be resting on soda dispensing surface. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was put through wash, rinse, and sanitize process and placed within ice with the handle outside of ice. Ensure all in use utensil are properly stored to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer bucket to be at 0ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was remade and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure all sanitizer buckets are at the proper sanitation level.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: (Repeatx2) Observed ice accumulation around the hose in the walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, hose will be serviced. Ensure equipment is kept in good repair and is functioning at the manufacture’s standards.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed cook line microwave to soiled with food splash. Discussed with PIC, microwave will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces of equipment are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Proper use of restriction and exclusion
findings.comment:
Observed no restriction and exclusion paperwork to be present in facility during inspection. Discussed with PIC, inspector provided facility with the required paperwork. Ensure restriction and exclusion paperwork is kept within facility during all hours of operation.  

2-201.12: The PERSON IN CHARGE shall EXCLUDE or RESTRICT a FOOD EMPLOYEE from a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in accordance with Law  symptoms/diagnosis

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a CFPM present at the start of the inspection. A CFPM arrived shortly afterwards. Ensure that a CFPM is present to cover all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Observed an employee placing a personal drink on a shelf that stores clean dishes in the dish room. The activity was ceased. Suggested that employee place drink in a designated area away from clean dishes. Ensure that personal drinks are stored separate from food related items used for public consumption. 

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed lasagna to be stored below raw meats in the walk in cooler near the dish room. Discussed with PIC proper storage of RTE foods and raw meats. The lasagna was rearranged. PIC noted that the lasagna was mistakenly placed underneath the raw meats. Ensure that RTE foods are always stored above raw meats to avoid cross contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the sani bucket on the cook line to be about 5ppm (CL). The bucket’s solution was changed and tested again at 100ppm. Ensure that sani buckets are maintained and frequently changed to properly sanitize food contact surfaces. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled with food debris:
- Behind the blade on the slicing machine
- Mixing blades on the milkshake machine by the hot holding unit
- Mixing blades on the mixer used for beating omelette eggs

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed spaghetti sauce to be held at an improper temperature on the steam table along the cook line area. The sauce was probed at 127F. Discussed with main cooks and spaghetti sauce was transferred to stove top to be reheated. Sauce was probed again at 166F. All other foods on the steam table tempted between 135F - 160F. Ensure that TCFs are being held at 135F or above at all times. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed the only allergen training certification to be expired (July 2023). PIC mentioned that they will be taking the allergen training soon. Educational handouts for allergen training were available in the binder from previous inspection. Ensure that at least 1 CFPM is allergen certified.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
